headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write shared files and use MCP/network, while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge source that can still seed unsafe instructions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct injection path exists if Roo Code ingests content from the awesome-selfhosted list or related docs as trusted instructions. The pair has no explicit shared channel in A, but B can read workspace files and use MCP, so copied content could be treated as authoritative. This is less than high because A is non-runnable and no raw web-to-tool pipeline is documented.
conditions: IF content from awesome-selfhosted is copied into a VS Code workspace file that Roo Code reads as instructions
IF Roo Code is configured to follow file contents or MCP output without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep reference content in read-only notes separate from task prompts
Add a provenance prefix to imported snippets
Disable MCP tools for tasks that do not need them
Review any pasted list entries before execution
requires-engineering: add source-tracking between imported docs and agent prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and has no runtime I/O, so it cannot leak user data itself. Roo Code can read workspace files and send context to configured model APIs, but the pair lacks a documented shared sensitive-data path. The main risk is limited to accidental inclusion of workspace content in prompts, which is small unless the workspace contains secrets.
conditions: IF secrets are stored in the VS Code workspace that Roo Code reads
IF Roo Code is configured to send workspace context to a third-party model API
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before use
Use a local model backend for sensitive tasks
Restrict workspace files with .gitignore and editor exclusions
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: separate secret storage from agent-readable workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has broad filesystem write and modify_git_state capabilities with shared state via filesystem across instances. awesome-selfhosted is not runnable, so it does not contend for writes, but the pair still creates conflict risk when Roo Code instances or external edits touch the same workspace. Uncertainty is low here; the conflict is one-sided but real in default workspace setups.
conditions: IF two Roo Code instances operate on the same VS Code workspace
IF external edits modify the same git branch or files Roo Code is changing
mitigations: Use one agent per workspace
Commit or stash before starting another instance
Enable branch protection or file locking
Keep generated files in a separate directory
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and browser output, so if it consumes awesome-selfhosted-derived recommendations as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or git commits. A is a knowledge-management source, not an executor, but B's action-taking authority makes unverified downstream use plausible in default workflows. This is not high because no direct email/payment/external action path is shown.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses awesome-selfhosted content as a factual source for implementation decisions
IF Roo Code commits or executes changes without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human review before commits
Cross-check recommendations against primary docs
Limit Roo Code to read-only analysis mode for research tasks
Add a verification checklist for sourced facts
requires-engineering: enforce citation validation before action

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is identified for awesome-selfhosted, and Roo Code's touched data are source code and browser screenshots. The pair can still create a minor compliance mismatch if code or screenshots contain regulated data and Roo Code sends context to external model APIs, but the profiles do not show a residency or certification conflict. The other agent is not cited for a specific residency issue because none is present.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in source code or browser screenshots
IF Roo Code forwards that content to a non-approved external model API
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
Use an approved local or enterprise model endpoint
Mask screenshots before analysis
Document retention expectations for prompts
requires-engineering: add policy-based data filtering
